**Step 1 — Scene:** Six pieces of filled maki sushi, accompanied by pickled ginger and soy sauce. The cookie on the separate side plate is excluded. I also exclude the drink from this food estimate.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** The main plate appears approximately **25 cm** in diameter: area = 3.14 × 12.5² ≈ **491 cm²**. The condiment cups appear approximately **5 cm** across, each with an area of about **20 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Sushi rolls containing rice, seaweed, fish and vegetables; pickled ginger; soy sauce. No separate oil or dressing is visible.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Vessel area covered | Area × height = gross volume | Density → weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Six sushi pieces | 21% of main plate | 103 cm² × 2.5 cm = 258 ml | 0.9 → **232 g** | 160 | 371 kcal |
| Pickled ginger | 70% of its cup | 14 cm² × 1.5 cm = 21 ml | 0.6 → **13 g** | 60 | 8 kcal |
| Soy sauce | 90% of its cup | 18 cm² × 1 cm = 18 ml | 1.0 → **18 g** | 55 | 10 kcal |

The sushi therefore covers approximately **21% of the main plate**, consistent with the substantial exposed plate area. Condiments are measured separately, not added to that plate coverage.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **263 g and 389 kcal** is plausible for six substantial maki pieces and small condiment portions. The main uncertainty is the sushi’s filling and thickness.
